correctness.rationale: Writing A,B,C for the three successive generators gives differences B−A=3n+1, C−B=3n+4, C−A=6n+5. Reducing 2A and 2B modulo the adjacent differences proves both adjacent gcds divide 2; the outer gcd divides 35 because it divides odd 6n+5 and n(3n−1), whose individual common divisors with 6n+5 divide 5 and 7. Therefore the triple has gcd one. For n≥6 one has A<B<C<2A, hence minimality; direct check handles n=3,4 and the redundant C at n=2,5. A symmetric minimally three-generated semigroup must have a two-generated gluing across a pair with gcd d>1. For n≥71, the adjacent-pair candidates 2C=xA+yB and 2A=xB+yC are excluded by comparing x+y with 2 and using 3A>2C and C<2A. For the outer pair the two strict inequalities in the frozen proof hold at 71 and increase thereafter. They force x+y=d in dB=xA+yC, so (2y−d)(6n+5)=−3d while 6n+5>105≥3d. Exact independent modular-inverse enumeration in 3≤n≤70 excluding 5 gave precisely (n,d,x,y)=(3,2,4,1),(40,35,7,27). For normalized coprime (u,v) and target w, take the least j≥0 with vj≡w mod u; this j minimizes vj among all permitted coefficients, so membership is equivalent to vj≤w. A second independent test marked members k by the recurrence k−A or k−B or k−C in S, starting with 0 and stopping after A consecutive marked integers; adding A then proves that no later gaps exist. Through n=70 it yielded symmetric indices 2,3,5,40, with F=43,133,1699,258529. The standard three-generator symmetry/CI equivalence and the two-generator hypersurface presentation give the CI claim over any field.
